failures.criterion: A7 (R6) - every acceptance line of dispatch://INFRA-261's approved spec (version 14) passes, whose third line reads: every Dispatch view that reads the agent list (the Agents page, an issue's and a document's subscribers, mention suggestions, an agent's conversation page, route status) shows a refilling state while the listener refills
failures.evidence: The refilling state does not cross Dispatch server processes: only the process that made the listener call shows it, and every other process shows an unreachable listener for as long as that process's answer is the stored one. Driven on the real surface with two real `envoy-dispatch` processes on one database, one real listener and one real natsd, all built from this head (/legion/scratch/tmp/tester/two-dispatch-refill.sh; log /legion/scratch/tmp/tester/refill3.log). With NATS stopped until the listener answered `503 {"code":"refilling"} Retry-After: 5`: process A, which fetched, read `{"route_status":"unknown","route_status_reason":"refilling"}` and answered `GET /api/v1/agents` with `503 {"code":"ENVOY_REFILLING"}`; process B, reading the row A stored, read `{"route_status":"unknown","route_status_reason":"unreachable"}` and answered agents `503 {"code":"ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE","error":"envoy listener unavailable: the listener did not answer Dispatch's last read of its sessions"}`. It is not one process's five-second window: after B's own fetch stored its silence, A flipped to `unreachable` too, so under a sustained refill with two processes serving reads each shows the unreachable marker most of the time. The issue page renders the two apart (`issue-route-refilling` with "The Envoy listener is refilling its agent list" against `issue-route-unreachable`, packages/dispatch/web/src/features/issue/IssueHeader.tsx:535 and RouteReach.tsx:111), so a person reading the page is told the listener is unreachable while it is refilling. The cause is recorded in the code the round shipped: `remember` (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_route_status.go:281-297) says the stored row records only `answered`, so a stored silence reads as `model.RouteReasonUnreachable`; the implementer's handoff lists it under openQuestions as needing a migration. Red test: `TestARefillOneServerMetIsARefillOnTheOther` in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_route_status_test.go, which fails at this head with `GET /issues/TEST-1 reads route_status=unknown route_holder=null route_status_reason=unreachable, want ... refilling` under `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL="$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN" go test -count=1 -run TestARefillOneServerMetIsARefillOnTheOther ./internal/dispatch/api/`.

failures.criterion: A6 - "for a session whose record the reaper deleted at the horizon, a send after a listener restart is refused with a text that says the listener does not know that time"
failures.evidence: The refusal says nothing about the time: it omits the field. Driven on the real listener (/legion/scratch/tmp/tester/states-adversarial.sh, log /legion/scratch/tmp/tester/adv2.log). Before the restart the refusal was `404 {"error":"no live session ses_adv_reaped_12111","state":"gone","last_seen":1793575549679}`; after the listener was restarted it was `404 {"error":"no live session ses_adv_reaped_12111","state":"gone"}` - `last_seen` absent, and no text in its place. A sender cannot tell a session this listener watched reach the gone horizon from one it has never heard of, which is the distinction the clause exists for, and `lastSeenOf` (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api.go:101-111) documents the zero as "not known" without any caller saying so. Red test: `TestARefusalThatCannotNameTheLastRegistrationSaysSo` in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/session_state_test.go, which fails at this head with `the refusal reads "no live session ses_reaped_before_the_restart" and says nothing about this listener not knowing when ... last registered` under `cd packages/envoy && go test -count=1 -run TestARefusalThatCannotNameTheLastRegistrationSaysSo ./cmd/listener/`.

failures.criterion: A6 - "A Legion role's Oh My Pi process, and a Legion role's Claude Code process, killed with SIGKILL under its worker shim, is gone within 10 seconds"
failures.evidence: Unproven by the round and not reachable from this pod, so it is reported rather than passed. The pod proof's check 6 measures a plain SIGKILL to a session's own process, which is gone at the horizon (90 s measured), not the daemon's clean stop; no check of scripts/e2e/envoy-session-states.sh starts a daemon, a worker shim or a launcher, and the implementer's A6 proof entry does not claim the clause. The clean stop itself is wired - supervise.Machine.died -> sessionGone -> Deps.SessionGone (packages/daemon/internal/supervise/machine.go:1082-1108) -> cleanSessionStop's DELETE /v1/sessions/<id> (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/daemon.go:1112-1138) - and packages/daemon/internal/supervise/sessiongone_test.go pins that it follows the probe's verdict under both runtimes, but a committed test is a regression lock, not proof of the ten seconds. The two surfaces that would drive it are both out of reach here: the tmux runtime needs tmux, which this worker image does not carry (`command -v tmux` finds none, and config.go takes only `tmux` and `kubernetes`), and the Kubernetes runtime would need a daemon with cluster credentials this pod does not hold, or killing a role of the live INFRA tree, which is not mine to do. The architect decides: either a surface is built for it (a devbox run of scripts/e2e/stage2-tmux-supervision.sh extended to read the listener after the kill), or the clause is restated against a surface this tree can drive.

notDriven: A4's "a daemon notice to the role, written during the stop, reaches the session within 3 minutes after SIGCONT" and "a READY packet to a merge-queue role whose holder is stopped the same way is kept and delivered after SIGCONT": read rather than driven, for the same reason as A6's worker-shim clause - no surface here starts a daemon. Both paths keep the work: `mergeQueue` and the notice executor return the error for `notify.ErrHolderUnresponsive` (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/outbox.go:714-724, notice_exceptions.go:174-175) rather than standing it in with a Dispatch message, and `retryBackoff` caps at 64 s (outbox.go:404-412), so the first attempt after the session answers again is inside the three minutes.

A8's "a new plugin against a listener without the change shows its sessions as live": read rather than driven. The wire schema defaults a missing `state` to live (`WireStateSchema = SessionStateSchema.default("live")`, packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:36), which is the whole of that clause.

A3's "a topic send with receipts ... names the stopped one": the name is the listener's own log line, which this round observed - `listener publish topic skipped an unresponsive session` with the session id, `delivery_status: skipped`, `reason: unresponsive` and `last_seen` - and the confirmed path counts an unresponsive recipient skipped rather than failed (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/confirmed.go:444-464, 128-134). The publish answer itself carries no recipient list to name it in.
